records.reason: Measure m205 at 2/1 and 100 ul to bridge its strong 1/1-to-5/1 transition and calibrate onset and finish separately; measured 1/1 and 2/1 points 1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7 and 91b6bda771851a5c78ac are already substantially later than prediction.
Probe a halogenated aldehyde at 5/1 and moderate loading to test structural transfer in an acceptor-poor aromatic family.
Measure a chlorinated ketone at 50/1 to extend high-ratio coverage and compare baseline retention against related aromatic scaffolds.
Explore a weakly anchored donor-containing scaffold at 2/1 with PE loading solvent, adding graph-level coverage outside the dominant carbonyl families.
Establish an EA-rich aromatic aldehyde control to constrain compact onset and finish behavior in a sparsely anchored scaffold.
Measure a bromo-chlorotoluene at 5/1 as a low-polarity halogenated control for ordinary compact elution.
Probe a high-ratio fused aryl ether scaffold where heteroatom placement and ring topology may matter beyond global polarity descriptors.
Establish an EA-rich m104 point at 100 ul as a local control for severe finish errors in related aminobenzoate conditions.
Measure m128 at 5/1 and 100 ul between sulfur-ketone anchors 117874b15293a4b5e3e1 and 40d5f6dbba8de32e9852 to test whether its response is smooth or sharply transitional.
Measure m72 at 1/1 to anchor the lower-strength side of its broad finish response, complementing measured points 65e1a598d00339bec2f8 and 89425cdfb228a6ebf75d.
Add an EA-rich m121 point as a compact aromatic ether control for condition-response transfer across low-polarity oxygenated scaffolds.
Probe a high-ratio difluorobenzaldehyde scaffold at low sample loading as a compact halogenated-aldehyde control outside the largest carbonyl-rich tails.
Measure a low-ratio phenoxy ester at 100 ul to add a weakly anchored ester environment and constrain ordinary-regime predictions.
Measure a fluorobenzonitrile at 5/1 with PE loading to test acceptor-rich aromatic transfer and finish calibration outside aldehydes and ketones.
Add an m80 high-ratio point at high loading to compare compact ester behavior against measured loading-sensitive carbonyl tails.
Measure m12 at 50/1 and 100 ul to extend its high-ratio response between existing lower-ratio measurements.
Measure m81 at 20/1 and 100 ul to test whether its finish remains compact after the measured 10/1 loading contrast 7d402b3fad455f06fe68 and eb6c235e6ed90084bfc9.
Establish a low-ratio m49 control with a 50-ul sample, separating ordinary aldehyde retention from large late tails in multifunctional scaffolds.
Measure a low-ratio anisole ketone at 100 ul to add an oxygenated aromatic control for baseline and finish calibration.
Measure m100 at 5/1 with PE loading and 150 ul, adding an ester control in a high-ratio regime where loading and finish coupling remain uncertain.
Fill the m30 5/1-to-50/1 gap at 10/1 under fixed loading. The measured pair 595ef9e60d54ebad4071 and 605436d35600502e8c2e shows a much steeper response than predicted.
Extend a dibromobenzaldehyde scaffold to 20/1 at low loading, testing whether halogenated aldehydes remain compact or develop a finish tail.
Establish an EA-rich phenolic ether control at 0/1 to constrain ordinary donor-containing aromatic behavior before weaker elution.
Measure a pyridyl diarylamine at 5/1 to add a basic heteroaromatic environment and test structural transfer across acceptor-rich scaffolds.
Measure an isopropyl benzophenone at 1/1 as a compact aryl-ketone control for baseline onset and finish calibration.
Add m185 at 2/1 and 150 ul to provide an intermediate-ratio point for a difluorobenzaldehyde family and compare with high-ratio behavior.
Measure a fused lactone at 0/1 and 100 ul to broaden fused-ring structural coverage and test whether ring oxygen changes finish behavior.
Probe a beta-ketoester at 2/1 and 50 ul, adding a low-loading carbonyl-rich control to distinguish ordinary finish growth from extreme tails.
Measure an iodobenzoate at 0/1 with a large loading plug as a high-density ester control for loading-feature transfer.
Measure a dibenzyl diketone at 0/1 and low loading to add a compact multi-carbonyl structural anchor before weaker-eluent conditions.
Measure m70, a long-chain aryl ketone, at 0/1 and 150 ul as a lipophilic control for compact retention and finish behavior.
Measure a brominated acid derivative at 10/1 and 150 ul to add a polar carbonyl control with distinct loading amount and high-ratio conditions.

hypotheses.content: Weak elution at high PE/EA ratios can produce sharp, scaffold-specific retention transitions that the current model underestimates for several carbonyl-rich and multifunctional families; a global late-retention correction would be unsafe.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate and high-ratio labels can teach where V1 and V2 transitions begin and prevent the model from averaging compact and long-tail scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do carbonyl-rich and ester controls show transferable transition locations, or must correction remain local to molecular environment?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, sample volume, and loading-plug volume affect retention conditionally and can shift V1 and V2 differently; apparent loading laws are nonlinear and scaffold-dependent.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading controls can teach interactions between loading features and chemical structure instead of allowing one scaffold response to dominate the global fit.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do loading shifts transfer across ester, ketone, and sulfur-containing scaffolds when ratio and plug solvent are controlled?

hypotheses.content: V2 finish behavior requires separate calibration from V1 onset, especially for compounds with compact onset but solvent- or loading-dependent tails.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-specific response curves can reduce V2 error without shifting already accurate onset predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can compact controls and intermediate-ratio labels locate finish growth while preserving local onset calibration?

hypotheses.content: Sulfide, sulfoxide, and sulfur-containing carbonyl scaffolds have local retention and solvent-response behavior that is not captured reliably by acceptor count or TPSA alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Sulfur controls can improve graph-level transfer and distinguish sulfur-specific shifts from ordinary solvent effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do sulfur and thiophene controls share a response pattern after loading is controlled?

hypotheses.content: Local substitution and ring environment control ratio-response curvature among aryl ketones and fused ketones; descriptor-matched compounds can occupy different retention regimes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched aryl-ketone and fused-ring controls provide local structural examples instead of one generic correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which parts of the m30 and m35 weak-eluent slopes transfer, and which depend on substitution position or ring topology?

feedback_interpretation: Recent measurements favor scaffold-specific weak-eluent transition repair. The m30 and m35 high-ratio points were much later than predicted, while the m180 pair was accurate, so a broad late-retention correction remains unsafe. Loading contrasts for m125, m92, and m81 continue to support conditional loading effects. m197 and m182 further support direct V2 calibration at intermediate conditions.
batch_rationale: The batch combines matched or adjacent condition probes for high-impact failure families with compact controls spanning esters, aldehydes, ketones, sulfur compounds, heteroaromatics, and fused rings. Loading and plug-volume variation is retained in several candidates, while high-ratio and EA-rich conditions constrain solvent-response curvature. These labels should improve V1/V2 generalization by separating scaffold-specific tails from ordinary compact rows and by exposing interactions between chemistry and recorded loading features.
